title: Retail Investors Buy $550M in US Tech Stocks Before AI Selloff

tickers.name: CoreWeave, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Mom-and-pop investors increased their holdings in AI-related shares and memory chipmakers through Oct. 21, pushing weekly purchases of technology ETFs to 2.1 standard deviations above their historical average. The buying was concentrated in AI infrastructure and neocloud providers such as CoreWeave.

Retail traders spent nearly $550 million on U.S. technology stocks during that period, their largest weekly expenditure in at least two years. This surge in buying preceded a 6.7% drop in the semiconductor index ($SOX) on Oct. 22, the index's worst daily performance since June 23 and part of a 19.5% decline since Oct. 6.

selectedTweets.text:
Retail investors doubled down on AI stocks just before the SELLOFF:

Mom-and-pop investors bought +$550 million in US technology stocks over the last week, their largest weekly purchase in at least 2 years.

This was driven by purchases of semiconductor stocks, memory manufacturers, and neocloud providers such as CoreWeave, $CRWV.

Retail buying of individual technology stocks over the past week reached its highest level since July, while inflows into tech ETFs surged to their 2nd-highest EVER.

Friday alone saw the largest single-day inflow into tech ETFs ever, pushing weekly purchases to 2.1 standard deviations above their historical average, with the Semiconductor ETF, $SMH, among the biggest beneficiaries. 

Meanwhile, the semiconductor index, $SOX, dropped -6.7% on Thursday, its largest daily decline since June 23rd. $SOXX  

$SOX is now down -19.5% since October 6th.

This is absolutely incredible.
